evidence: generated/src/textual/widgets/tabs.py:157-168 computes the label layout in cells (cell_len, cursor + span_width) but builds the row text with character length (padded = " " * left + tab.label + " " * right, :168)

generated/src/textual/widgets/tabs.py:183-190 then calls label_row.stylize(click_style, cursor, cursor + span_width) with those cell values. Rich Text.stylize takes character offsets, so this is wrong whenever a label has double-width characters

Example: Tabs([Tab("に月", "two"), Tab("March")], active_tab="two", tab_padding=1). The row is 13 cells but 11 characters. March's click span becomes chars 6-10, which draw at cells 8-12, so March's padding and 'M' (cells 6-7) do not activate it

The reference attaches the click metadata to each tab's own Text (reference tabs.py get_tab_labels, Style.from_meta on the padded label), so it has no offset problem. The underline's click ranges (tabs.py:190/198, cell-based in UnderlineBar) are correct, so only the label row is affected

Not a defect: the candidate's Escape path (tabs.py:401 `await self.app.set_focus(None)`) is correct where the reference's un-awaited call is not, since base App.set_focus is async (base src/textual/app.py:306). The reference's test_clickable_ranges expectations (spans[-2]/spans[-1] with @click meta, underline_bar.py:91-95) are satisfied by the candidate's span ordering
criteria.deficiency: Clicks on inactive tab labels are mapped with character offsets while layout is in cells (generated/src/textual/widgets/tabs.py:183-190). Any tab that follows a double-width-character label has its click region shifted by the extra cell count, so it does not match what is drawn. Fix by attaching the click style to each tab's own Text (as the reference does) or by converting cell positions to character indices. The candidate's tests do not cover wide characters, so this is not caught.
